title: Netflix Treats GPU Reliability as a Distributed Systems Problem
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/netflix-gpu-distributed-systems/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792576903003.jpg"/><p>Netflix has detailed how it is building a reliability platform for large-scale GPU training and inference, using layered health checks, automated remediation, and fault-tolerant training to keep jobs running despite hardware failures.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Netflix Titus Adds Single-Tenant VM Isolation for Containers
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/netflix-titus-kubernetes-microvm/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793268697529.jpg"/><p>Netflix has added single-tenant Titus, a mode that runs one task alone on its own right-sized EC2 instance. The Compute/Platform team still owns and patches the host, so application teams keep the same API and deployment path</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: Microsoft Retires Azure Deployment Environments with No Replacement Product
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ade-dev-box-retirement/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792499241111.jpg"/><p>Azure Deployment Environments retires on February 22, 2027 and Microsoft names no successor, telling teams to use Bicep or ARM templates directly. Microsoft Dev Box follows on September 18, 2028, pointed at Windows 365, which Microsoft says is not a one-to-one replacement. Remaining Dev Box workloads should expect deletion.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Bug0 Releases QA Agent to Automate Regression Testing With Cached Playwright Replays
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/bug0-agent-testing-cached-replay/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793286673185.jpg"/><p>QA Agent is a new source-available Playwright library for agentic browser regression testing. The agent associates test instructions expressed in natural language to actions on the user interface, caches those when appropriate for faster CI replays, remapping them to test specifications when the user interface changes. Verification is based on multi-model consensus and vision model evaluations.</p> <i>By Bruno Couriol</i>

title: Datadog Builds a Specialist AI Model for SRE Investigations
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/datadog-scout-sre-model/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793038066919.jpg"/><p>Datadog has released Scout, a model trained to investigate production problems. It runs inside Bits Investigation, the company's AI SRE product, where it can pick up an alert, look through telemetry and suggest what caused the problem. Datadog engineers and a small number of customers are using it in a closed preview.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: Presentation: Wrangling Telemetry at Scale: A Guide to Self-Hosted Observability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/self-hosted-observability-stack-tradeoffs/en/mediumimage/colin-douch-medium-1791450600829.jpeg"/><p>Colin Douch shares battle-tested strategies for building and scaling self-hosted observability stacks. He explains how to effectively correlate metrics, structured logs, and distributed traces using open-source tooling like Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics, and Jaeger, while navigating the engineering trade-offs of avoiding SaaS vendor lock-in.</p> <i>By Colin Douch</i>

title: Microsoft's October Security Update Fixes 1,400+ Vulnerabilities, One Exploited in the Wild
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/microsoft-october-2026-patch/en/headerimage/microsoft-october-patch-1793129871505.jpeg"/><p>Microsoft's latest monthly security update addresses 1415 vulnerabilities across multiple products. One vulnerability affecting Windows Shell has been exploited in the wild, while 85 are classified as critical. Affected products include Windows OS, Office, Exchange, .NET, Edge, as well as potentially Hyper-V and Azure components.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Cloudflare Opens Quicksilver to Customers as Workers KV Instant, Inside a 1 MB Envelope
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has put Quicksilver, the internal key-value store behind nearly every request it serves, into private beta as a Workers KV mode. Reads resolve in 1.62 ms at p99 against 287 ms for classic KV. The constraints decide the use case: 10,000 keys, one megabyte per namespace, and one write per namespace per second.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Uber Moves beyond CPU Cores with Performance-Aware Scheduling for Stateful Workloads
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/uber-cpu-stateful-workloads/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792576315045.jpg"/><p>Uber has introduced Normalized Compute Units (NCUs) to make CPU allocation more consistent across its highly heterogeneous server fleet.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: AWS Shows Use of AI Agents to Triage Linux Kernel CVEs
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-ai-agents-linux-kernel-cves/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793031817205.jpg"/><p>Engineers from Amazon Web Services (AWS) have described how the team that maintains the Linux kernel for EC2 infrastructure handles kernel CVEs. The process combines an automated filter, an AI agent and human review. The team also argues that it needs to move to newer long-term-support (LTS) kernels, as older branches collect fixes that are never backported.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: Developers Reporting Double-Digit Weekly Time Savings from AI Fell from 68% to 26%
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/atlassian-devex-2026/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793026389174.jpg"/><p>Atlassian’s State of Developer Experience 2026 finds the share of developers saving ten or more hours a week with AI dropped from 68% to 26% year over year, while only 28% report noticeably less friction than before AI. Engineering leaders report spending more time managing and correcting AI output than developers do.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: AGNTCon + MCPCon 2026: Agentic AI Foundation Adds Four Projects as MCP Turns to Security
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/agntcon-mcpcon-2026/en/headerimage/agntcon-header-1792936265463.jpg"/><p>At AGNTCon + MCPCon North America 2026, the Agentic AI Foundation added OpenSandbox, Open Responses, Agent Skills, and OpenEnv, reaching ten projects in its first year. Keynotes from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and UC Berkeley focused on MCP in production, security, and agents with their own identities.</p> <i>By Andrew Hoblitzell</i>

title: OpenTofu 1.13 Lets Module Authors Reduce Unknown Values at Plan Time
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/opentofu-1-13-unknown-values/en/headerimage/header-1792823798248.jpeg"/><p>OpenTofu 1.13 adds convert and assume... functions that let module authors give the planner type and value hints for unknown values, so more expressions resolve during tofu plan. If a value unknown during planning later violates a guarantee, OpenTofu reports an error during apply.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: Readyon Builds Four Layer Tenant Isolation for Multi Tenant Amazon EKS
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>ReadyOn has detailed a four-layer tenant isolation architecture for its Harmony platform on Amazon EKS. The design combines Kubernetes namespaces, dedicated Karpenter node pools, VPC security groups, and per-tenant Aurora databases, with controls evaluated against a 10-stage multi-tenant threat model focused on cross-tenant access and lateral movement.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Cloudflare’s Auto Router Rates Each Request for Stakes, from the Most Recent Turns
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-auto-router/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792492628413.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has released Auto Router in public beta through AI Gateway, picking a model per request from a classifier that scores complexity, ambiguity, stakes and context dependence. Cloudflare’s own benchmark puts it ten points below Claude Opus 5.5 on success rate at a third of the cost, and practitioners have questioned how stakes survive a long agent session.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>
